W7221770042.abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most urgent global public health threats, especially in low- and middle-income countries. In 2019, bacterial AMR was estimated to have directly caused approximately 1.27 million deaths and to have been associated with 4.95 million deaths worldwide. Rapid identification of resistant infections is important, yet established diagnostics are very slow. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized microbiology and infectious disease diagnostics. This review explores the space of AI-enabled diagnostics for AMR detection and characterization. Methods: This literature review was conducted from January to September 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and other electronic databases with keywords including "AI," "AMR," "deep learning," "genomic diagnostics," and "point-of-care (POC) testing." Following screening and full-text assessment, 67 Peer-reviewed articles and systematic reviews were included to support the synthesis presented in the manuscript, while non-peer-reviewed articles and studies lacking direct AI relevance were excluded. Titles and abstracts were screened before full-text review. Results: AI-enhanced diagnostics were reported to shorten turnaround time for AMR detection with promising but heterogeneous predictive performance; for example, pooled estimates across antimicrobial stewardship applications indicate an area under the curve of approximately 0.72. They also support improving antimicrobial stewardship and enable early therapeutic optimization in laboratory and POC settings, enabling real-time clinical decision-making. Despite these achievements, evidence for direct improvements in patient outcomes and routine bedside effectiveness remains limited. Conclusion: AI-driven diagnostic tools represent a promising strategy to bridge laboratory innovation and bedside application in combating AMR. The tools have the capacity to improve patient outcomes and enhance antimicrobial stewardship as they can accurately detect resistance patterns and support real-time clinical decisions. However, long-term sustainability, long-term success, and global impact can be achieved by continued validation, regulatory alignment, and equitable implementation across diverse healthcare settings.

W7221797899.abstract: Diffusion language models reconstruct masked tokens in parallel, offering an alternative to autoregressive generation. Yet their Transformer backbones typically carry visible evidence and evolving masked predictions through a single residual stream. We equip masked diffusion models with multiple residual streams that persist through depth and adaptive routing between them, then investigate how they support these complementary roles. On the pretraining task, two streams reduce reconstruction perplexity by 5.71% on validation data and 5.13% on average across external corpora compared with standard residual connections. We observe that, without predefined roles, visible and masked positions learn distinct routing patterns. Causal interventions show that this distinction organizes read and write routing, while token-specific write strength remains important within each role. Guided by these findings, a model trained with role-conditioned routing recovers half the validation gain from adding a second stream. State interventions explain the benefit of the additional stream: it preserves early token representations for later reuse while evidence accumulates at masked positions. This mechanism recurs at a larger model scale, showing how persistent streams support context preservation alongside prediction refinement.

W7221818493.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Automated semantic classification of radiology reports can enhance clinical workflows and research, but often relies on language- and task-specific models, limiting scalability. This study aims to evaluate and improve the 0-shot baseline performance of open-weight large language models (LLMs) in the semantic classification of free-text magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A corpus of 1385 reports from a single neuroradiology center was used to assess four LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, Magistral-Small-2509, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) of comparable scale (∼20-35B parameters). The brain MRI reports were labeled as Pathological or Non-Pathological, with the Pathological ones further classified into five diagnostic categories (Neoformation, Vascular, Inflammation/Infection, Neurodegenerative, Other). The LLMs were evaluated using zero- and few-shot prompting with majority-vote aggregation. Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) fine-tuning was then applied to the best-performing model across multiple configurations. Performance was assessed using Macro F1, Micro F1, Precision, Recall, and Exact Match Accuracy. RESULTS: The binary classification task achieved a Macro F1 score of 0.84 on the best-performing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model, while multilabel classification reached 0.81. Majority voting (MV) outperformed individual-set predictions. QLoRA fine-tuning yielded a Macro F1 score of 0.83 on the multilabel task; the improvement over the 0-shot baseline was statistically supported for Macro F1, Micro F1, Macro Precision, and Exact Match, whose bootstrap 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, but not for Macro Recall. Fine-tuning and few-shot prompting strategies are complementary, with neither consistently outperforming the other. Error analysis showed that the models struggled with borderline annotation cases and often missed secondary labels. CONCLUSION: Open-weight LLMs demonstrate strong capability for neuroradiology report classification without extensive task-specific training. Fine-tuning further improves performance, supporting integration into scalable semantic radiology data pipelines. However, the present evidence comes from a single Italian center without external validation, and the fine-tuning gain was estimated on a small held-out test set, for which the Macro F1 improvement, though statistically significant, has a confidence interval with a lower bound close to zero. In this light, the approach is best positioned as an internal indexing and semantic-retrieval tool, supporting faster report retrieval, structured cohort identification, internal audit, and scalable phenotyping for neuroradiology research and data warehousing, as well as efficient active-learning strategies, with broader generalizability requiring additional external multicentre validation before clinical deployment.

W7221871007.abstract: The circular built environment is characterized by dynamic building lifecycles, driven by heterogeneous material flows, iterative operational conditions, and multiple stakeholders. These requirements closely align with advances in emerging agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, enabling autonomous task decomposition, multi-tool reasoning, and feedback-driven adaptation. Despite rapid progress in autonomous multi-agent systems and digital twin (DT) intelligence, the integration of agentic AI into the circular built environment remains in its early stages. This study proposes an automated Level of Development (LoD) maturity assessment framework to evaluate the readiness of agentic AI workflows for circular construction applications. A two-phase systematic literature review was conducted to construct three research domains representing (1) agentic AI in the built environment, (2) circular construction, and (3) BIM/DT-based lifecycle digitalization. Cross-domain mapping revealed strong coupling between circularity and AI-enabled BIM/DT research, a developing trend between agentic AI and digitalization, and a limited intersection between agentic AI and circularity. The maturity classifications were mapped onto a LoD 100–500 scale, ranging from single-agent systems to autonomous frameworks. Initial maturity scores were generated using a large language model based on a six-dimensional (D1–D6) agentic maturity rubric covering agency structure, tool integration, reasoning depth, adaptivity, autonomy, and environmental data resolution. The outputs were assessed using an LLM-assisted consistency-checking procedure across rubric dimensions. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach to assess the readiness of agentic AI systems for the development of autonomous circular construction workflows

W7222255865.abstract: This study presents an integrated methodology combining machine learning, atomic-scale design, and experimental validation to develop high-entropy spinel ferrite nanomaterials (Co0.5Ni0.5Fe2O4) for advanced energy storage applications. Electrochemical evaluations revealed hybrid charge-storage behavior merging capacitive and diffusion-controlled mechanisms, with cyclic voltammetry showing a significant increase in current density at higher scan rates, confirming large surface area and quasi-reversible redox reactions. Galvanostatic charge-discharge tests exhibited distinct voltage plateaus characteristic of Faradaic processes, with a specific capacitance strongly dependent on current density; Coulombic efficiency reached 95% at 1 A/g but declined to 55% at 10 A/g due to irreversible side reactions and ion trapping. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy demonstrated a low charge-transfer resistance (~4 Ω) and a Warburg diffusion line with a 35° slope, indicating a porous, rough surface and battery-type behavior rather than ideal supercapacitor performance. The absence of a second semicircle confirmed electrical homogeneity and high surface activity. Overall, the nanomaterial exhibited excellent electronic conductivity facilitated by cobalt and nickel ions within the spinel lattice, making it a promising positive electrode candidate for next-generation batteries and supercapacitors. This work underscores that merging machine learning-driven predictions with precise experimental synthesis offers an efficient pathway to accelerate the discovery of advanced energy storage materials by correlating atomic-scale structural distortions with macroscopic electrochemical performance.

W7222575690.abstract: Background. Transcriptomic data show which genes are active in cells and tissues. Machine-learning and deep-learning methods use these data to classify samples, integrate different datasets, and predict biological properties and treatment response. In oncology, a major challenge is transferring patterns identified in experimental models to tumor samples from patients. Objective. To critically synthesize current artificial-intelligence methods for transcriptomic analysis, with emphasis on oncology applications, transfer of models to patient data, and requirements for clinical validation. Materials and Methods. We performed a critical narrative review of primary studies and methodological papers and additionally described the authors' publication sample for 2021–2026. The literature review was updated through August 13, 2026. Results. The most developed areas include single-cell data analysis, spatially resolved tumor diagnostics, and drug-response prediction. Independent comparative evaluations show that increasing model size and complexity does not guarantee better performance than simpler methods. Clinical translation requires accounting for cellular composition and technical differences between measurement batches, aligning experimental and clinical response measures, preventing information leakage, and performing external validation. Conclusion. Artificial intelligence should be viewed as a data-analysis tool rather than a substitute for experimental or clinical validation. Its value depends on data quality, correct task definition, and the ability to maintain performance in independent cohorts.

W7222794282.abstract: One of the common problems with LLMs (Large Language Models) is that they sometimes produce fluent text that deviates from the given source or from world knowledge, a phenomenon known as hallucination.In search engines, healthcare, legal and enterprise applications, the need for factually reliable LLM is now placed in the first place of the agenda of both the researchers and practitioners.This paper reviews the causes of hallucination, categorizes hallucination detection into reference-based and black-box families and examines different categories of approaches for mitigating hallucination from the training-time, retrieval-augmented, decoding-time and post-hoc verification.In addition to this survey, we conduct a comparative study of six mitigation setups and five detection techniques for short-form question answering and long-form generation.The rate of hallucination decreases by about 66.7% from direct prompting for long-form generation by retrieval-augmented generation and post-hoc verification, and by smaller and complementary amounts by contrastive decoding and chain-of-verification.Retrieval-grounded factual-precision scoring outperforms consistency-based black-box detection approaches, which rely on no knowledge of the model's inner workings, when it comes to sentence-level detection accuracy among the detection methods.We find that none of the single-behaviour systems are found to be capable of eliminating hallucination and that the most reliable systems are those that use a training-time or decoding-time intervention followed by an external, retrievalgrounded verification step.

W7222825169.abstract: This research paper presents a proposed framework for Autonomous AI Agents for Software Development, focusing on the transition from code generation to automated testing, debugging, and software verification. The paper introduces a modular, role-based architecture consisting of a planner agent, context retriever, coder agent, tester agent, debugger agent, and reviewer agent. These components work together through a bounded Plan-Code-Test-Repair workflow to understand software requirements, retrieve relevant code, generate changes, execute tests, diagnose failures, and improve code quality. The proposed framework emphasizes functional correctness, automated test generation, repository-level issue resolution, secure tool execution, human approval, and auditability. It also outlines an evaluation protocol using established benchmarks and metrics to assess code correctness, test quality, efficiency, cost, reliability, and security. This work synthesizes existing research on large language models, reasoning-and-acting agents, self-debugging, multi-agent systems, and automated software testing. It provides a conceptual architecture and evaluation plan for future implementation and experimentation. No implemented system or benchmark results are claimed in this paper. The research aims to support the development of more reliable, secure, and transparent AI-assisted software engineering systems.

W7223003673.abstract: Sycophancy, where an LLM becomes overly agreeable, deferential, or flattering toward the user, has been identified as a major failure mode.While post-training has been implicated as a cause, how it internally gives rise to sycophantic behavior remains insufficiently understood.Post-training transforms the model's output from text completion into utterances directed toward an addressee, thereby giving the output addressivity.We hypothesize that the accompanying pressure to follow the addressee's instructions and align with their preferences links this addressivity to sycophancy.To test this, we use Sparse Autoencoders to extract addressivity directions from pre-trained and posttrained models and examine their relationship with sycophancy.Steering models with addressivity directions can amplify or suppress sycophancy, and this effect is observed only in posttrained models.Furthermore, comparing the internal mechanisms of both model types confirms that the association between addressivity and sycophancy is strengthened through posttraining.Finally, through a controlled posttraining experiment, we find that models are sycophantic not toward a specific addressee but toward any recognized addressee, suggesting that the presence of an addressee, rather than the addressee's identity, is what elicits sycophancy.

W7223073274.abstract: The increasing use of digital platforms, cloud services, and interconnected information systems has created a growing need for intelligent identity pattern discovery while maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of sensitive data. Conventional centralized data mining approaches require information from multiple sources to be collected in a common repository, increasing the risks of unauthorized access, data exposure, and privacy violations. Federated learning offers an alternative by enabling multiple organizations or distributed clients to collaboratively train machine learning models without directly exchanging their raw data. This study proposes a privacy-preserving framework for identity pattern discovery using federated learning. The proposed framework analyses identity-related behavioural characteristics, such as authentication events, login frequency, access patterns, and deviations from established user behaviour. Local models are trained at participating clients, while a central aggregation server combines model updates to develop a collaborative global model. Additional privacy mechanisms, including secure aggregation and differential privacy, are considered to reduce the risk of information leakage from model updates. The framework is designed to evaluate identity pattern discovery performance, privacy protection, communication overhead, and model robustness under distributed and heterogeneous data conditions. Performance can be assessed using precision, recall, F1-score, and detection accuracy, together with appropriate privacy and computational measures. The proposed approach aims to support trustworthy identity analytics in distributed environments, although its practical effectiveness must be established through empirical evaluation.

W7223076225.abstract: The development of language agents is leading to the creation of new standards for multi-agent systems. Many such standards, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol, and the Universal Tool Calling Protocol (UTCP), enable agents to interact with Web-based systems, resulting in the creation of an Agentic Web. Hypermedia is a core feature of the Web that enables users to discover information at run time, and has been used to allow agents to interact with Web services and physical devices in open Web environments through hypermedia standards, such as the Web of Things (WoT) Thing Description. However, MCP and A2A do not natively define hypermedia controls, which introduces coupling between agents and their environments, limiting their independent evolution in open environments. Building on prior work about hypermedia multi-agent systems, we develop a uniform hypermedia interface applicable to different Agentic Web standards. This interface enables agents to discover and interact with entities of different types. This interface relies on signifiers, which are hypermedia descriptions of affordances. We provide automatic generation of signifiers for MCP tools, A2A agents, UTCP tools, and WoT Things. We propose a natural language based selection method for such signifiers so that agents perceive only contextually relevant signifiers. We expose each signifier perceived by an agent as an MCP tool that performs the action described by the signifier. Finally, we demonstrate and evaluate these concepts in a robotic lab environment.

W7223153968.abstract: Personalized medicine aims to provide healthcare based on the biological and clinicalcharacteristics of individual patients. Advancement in genomics has made it possible to identifygenetic modifications related to disease risk, drug response, and treatment outcomes, but interpretinglarge and complex datasets remains challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI) is useful in analyzinggenomic, clinical, and treatment-related information and connecting these data with clinicaldecisions. This review examines the role of AI in personalized medicine, with a focus on genomicanalysis, clinical decision support, and precision therapeutics. AI applications in genomic medicineinclude variant interpretation, disease-risk prediction, pharmacogenomics, and multi-omics analysis.AI-based clinical decision support system can assist in risk assessment, diagnosis, treatmentselection, and patient monitoring. In precision therapeutics, AI facilitates support in drug selection,dose optimization, treatment-response prediction, and treatment monitoring. The review alsodiscusses applications in cancer, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, neurological disorders, and rarediseases. Important challenges include data quality, privacy, algorithmic bias, explainability, clinicalvalidation, cost, and unequal access to advanced technologies. W7223201679.abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation. We test 450 configurations across eight benchmarks and corpora ranging from 5K to 200K documents. Three findings emerge. First, individually strong techniques from different phases of a RAG pipeline do not necessarily compose: three retrieval techniques predict a +47% combined improvement but deliver only +17% when used together. Second, component gains stack differently for retrieval and faithfulness, and optimizing one can hurt the other. Third, the best composition changes as the corpus grows: the combination that wins on a small corpus may not remain best at large scale. These findings show that gains measured in isolation are not reliable predictors of realistic performance, and that new RAG techniques should be tested with the full surrounding stack. We call on researchers to do so and supply LASAGNA to simplify these experiments.

W7223303594.abstract: AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making introduce significant challenges related to safety, alignment, accountability, and human oversight. Existing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and responsible AI approaches provide important foundations, but many remain fragmented across system design, governance, and operational deployment. This paper presents a Three-Pillar (3P) model and framework for developing safe and trustworthy AI agents through transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness. The framework defines an evolutionary path in which increasing agent autonomy is introduced through progressive validation, structured human oversight, and auditable operational controls. We further describe how the model supports agent lifecycle monitoring, decision traceability, escalation management, and human-agent collaboration within enterprise agentic environments. By integrating oversight principles with operational mechanisms, the proposed framework provides a practical foundation for deploying AI agents that remain aligned with human intent while enabling controlled progression toward higher autonomy.

W7223441405.abstract: AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. Eight primary queries and one overlapping name-variant query were executed through the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API on 5 December 2025. English-language publications within a 1989–2026 search window were screened for substantive AI or robotics relevance and an explicit Husserlian anchor. Of 5,594 retrieved records, 32 publications from 1990 to 2025 were included. Nine publications recovered by a post hoc PhilPapers check were charted separately using the existing codebook; they were not added to the formal corpus. The corpus clusters around embodied AI, AI epistemology, cognitive architectures, and machine consciousness, with a newer generative-AI cluster. Constitution, intentionality, horizonality, and the lifeworld recur prominently. Conceptual translation, critique, and agenda setting predominate within this sample. Methodological import or design guidance occurs in seven of the 32 publications and three of the nine external publications. That difference qualifies generalization of the quantitative balance. Across both sets, Husserlian uptake spans conceptual interpretation, methodological transfer, and architectural proposals. The synthesis shows how distinctions concerning temporality, embodiment, and evidence can structure design and evaluation questions, while separating the authors’ research proposals from the mapped findings.

W7223658084.abstract: Large language model agents that use tools could take on part of the electronic health record and desk work that occupies physicians' time, but in many hospitals the medical information systems run inside closed networks, so the model and the agent harness must also be inside the network. We designed, implemented, and deployed LLENS, a clinical support AI agent platform that runs inside the closed network of Hokkaido University Hospital on a single host with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the open-weight model Kimi K2.6 (~1 trillion parameters), and a web application rebuilt from Open WebUI. The harness has 10 components, including page image reading, full-text attachment input, a path-addressed document tree without a vector index, a network-isolated sandbox, artifact return, self-checking of generated output, subagents, and saved procedures. Kimi K2.6 was chosen from 3 open-weight candidates and scored 480/500 on the 2026 Japanese Medical Licensing Examination; it generated 119 tokens/s for a single user and served 16 concurrent requests at 908 tokens/s in total. On 180 questions over hospital documents (3 seeds each), mean accuracy was 10.7% with no documents, 81.3% with fixed retrieval (top 10 chunks of one lexical search), and 97.2% with interactive access, in which the model reads with document tools and the sandbox (15.9 percentage points above fixed retrieval, 95% CI 10.9-21.3); the difference lay in filtering/counting questions (16.7% vs 87.8%). In an automated test of 13 work scenarios (4 runs each), the expected components were triggered in all runs for 12, and 5 scenarios were run with synthetic data on the deployment host. The platform has run on the hospital network since September 14, 2026.

W7223672038.abstract: Understanding how firms allocate attention to industrial policies is crucial for advancing sustainable industrial transformation. However, existing approaches to identifying corporate policy attention are constrained by the lack of domain-specific semantic alignment in general-purpose large language models (LLMs). To address this limitation, this study develops a domain-adaptive large language model framework for enhancing policy-attention theme identification in the new energy vehicle (NEV) sector, a representative policy-driven emerging technological sector. The framework involves constructing an instruction-based dataset reflecting the nuances of corporate policy attention in the NEV domain, applying Low-Rank Adaptation fine-tuning to a general large language model to obtain the domain-specific ChatGLM-LoRA-NEVPR model, and conducting comprehensive objective, human, and intelligent evaluations. Experimental results show that the proposed model improves policy-attention recognition accuracy by approximately 12% compared with the baseline, while demonstrating higher semantic coherence and authenticity across multiple dimensions. Overall, this research provides a robust methodological foundation for applying adaptive large language model techniques to analyze corporate policy attention in the NEV industry and other strategically significant, policy-supported industrial contexts.

W7224179947.abstract: Current large language models perform nexttoken prediction under the implicit assumption that all tokens lie in a shared Euclidean embedding space, which treats every token uniformly.However, natural language contains rich structural relationships, including hierarchical, compositional, and cyclic patterns, which the flat geometry of Euclidean space cannot model well.To address this limitation, we propose rLLM (Riemannian Large Language Modeling), which introduces a token-adaptive positive-definite diagonal metric tensor into the LM head.This metric dynamically adjusts the local quadratic score for each hidden state and its context, allowing the model to better capture the relationships among tokens and prompts, with less than 0.01% additional parameters.We train rLLM from scratch across three different scales (2.8B to 5.0B parameters), covering the full pretraining, SFT, and RL pipeline.Extensive experiments show that rLLM improves Base CORE, a composite of 22 in-context learning tasks, by up to +2.5pp at the two smaller GPT scales and obtains higher ChatCORE at all three scales, with gains up to +3.0pp after RL.These results suggest that revisiting the geometric assumptions underlying token representations is a promising direction for building more expressive and capable language models.Code is available at https://github. com/digailab/riemannianllm.git.

W7224248885.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly act by generating, executing, and revising code, making code reasoning essential for understanding program state, diagnosing failures, and repairing behavior.Existing evaluations often measure end-to-end software engineering outcomes, obscuring which reasoning capabilities limit agents in complex, execution-grounded systems.We study this problem through Proof-of-Concept (PoC) generation, where an agent synthesizes an executable trigger that reproduces a reported crash or sanitizer failure.We instantiate this task in the Linux kernel, whose scale, statefulness, pointer-heavy value flow, memory layout, and concurrency stress long-horizon code reasoning.We decompose kernel PoC generation into four capabilities: state-machine reasoning, dynamic memory layout reasoning, value-flow reasoning, and concurrency reasoning.We build KPocInfra to emit branch-level execution telemetry and curate KPocBench, a benchmark of 181 reproducible Linux kernel KASAN cases from Syzbot.On KPocBench, state-machine and value-flow reasoning explain most failures, while capabilityscaffolded evidence improves the best success rate from 50% to 61% and moves 29 unsolved attempts deeper along vulnerable execution paths.These results position kernel PoC generation as a practical stress test for LLM code reasoning in large-scale systems software.

W7224353631.abstract: NLP Large Language Models have had a deep impact not only on research but also on society.However, there is one problem underlying their own nature which forbids them to be fully trusted and accountable: Hallucinations -a phenomenon that calls for a scientific account in the form of a theoretical model that represents the underlying rationale of how it emerges.In this paper, we present such a model.In the same spirit as in other fields proposing models of natural phenomena -such as rainfallor social phenomena -such as knowledge creation in organizations -we propose a theoretical model that serves to explain hallucinations by synthesizing in an abstract and structured framework how the interrelations and interactions of more than 50 factors give rise to this phenomenon helping us to better understand its complexity and idiosyncrasies.

W7224405109.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong reasoning ability but are constrained by outdated knowledge and hallucinations.Knowledge Graphs (KGs) can help mitigate these limitations by providing structured relational knowledge and capturing global multi-entity, multi-hop dependencies beyond linear text.However, existing KG-enhanced LLM reasoning methods mostly rely on hop-by-hop textual traversal, rather than making multi-hop decisions with a broader perspective as humans do, thus underusing the structural advantages of KGs.This leads to myopic exploration and fragmented reasoning, wasting effort on irrelevant entities while potentially missing critical ones.To address these limitations, we propose Foresight-on-Graph (FoG), a novel framework that introduces visual relation graphs to expand the reasoning horizon at each step.FoG enables Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to simultaneously attend to multi-entity, multi-hop contexts, supporting foresighted planning and more efficient graph exploration.To facilitate effective visual reasoning, we design relation-based fuzzy matching and union-find algorithms to filter out irrelevant relations and coarsen the graph, condensing subgraphs with millions of entities into compact relation graphs with only tens of nodes.Experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that FoG consistently outperforms existing methods while significantly improving reasoning efficiency.Code is available at https://github.com/hyworrywart/ FoG. K Use of AI AssistantsAI assistants were used for language polishing, editing suggestions, and checklist preparation.All technical content, claims, experiments, and final text were reviewed and verified by the authors.

W7224746293.abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. Our experiments show that frontier agents often produce approximately correct reconstructions but remain unreliable at exact reconstruction, particularly in molecular-state representation and workflow connectivity. Switching the underlying language model produced larger average performance differences than switching agent harnesses, with a statistically significant difference only for molecular-state reconstruction. Additional knowledge improved oligo-family recovery in a small pilot without improving mean molecular-workflow scores. Autonomous accumulation of procedural rules and cross-protocol examples showed non-monotonic validation performance and no mean held-out molecular-workflow improvement in the tested trajectory. These findings highlight the need for more controlled and verifiable approaches to scientific reasoning about molecular processes in complex experimental protocols.

W7224915175.abstract: The fast evolution of cyber threats in enterprise environments calls for a paradigm shift from reactive security mechanisms to proactive, intelligent and autonomous defense systems. The traditional cybersecurity frameworks are not up to the scale, complexity and sophistication of modern attacks, particularly in multi-cloud, hybrid and distributed infrastructures. This paper proposes an integrated framework of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI) and Knowledge-Driven Data Intelligence (KDDI) for enterprise cybersecurity transformation. Our proposed architecture comprises autonomous AI agents endowed with perception, reasoning, decision-making, and action capabilities, along with knowledge graphs and data-driven intelligence for improved situational awareness and threat mitigation. The framework provides adaptive, scalable and explainable security solutions using machine learning, reinforcement learning, graph analytics and real-time threat intelligence. Experimental evaluation shows improved accuracy of threat detection, shorter response time and increased resilience in comparison to the traditional methods. The results show the potential of agentic and knowledge-driven systems to construct next-generation cybersecurity infrastructures.

W7224996487.abstract: The ability to automatically distinguish academic from non-academic texts is an important need in higher education environments. This study aims to design and build a web application that implements the IndoBERT model to classify Indonesian texts into academic or non-academic categories with interpretable output accompanied by classification reasoning. The system is built end-to-end using the PyTorch and HuggingFace Transformers stack for modeling, FastAPI as the backend, and vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the user interface. The dataset was manually compiled with 209 samples (108 academic and 101 non-academic texts). Model fine-tuning was performed on Google Colab using a Tesla T4 GPU with a learning rate of 2×10⁻⁵, batch size of 16, and eval_loss-based early stopping. The system is also equipped with a zero-shot fallback module so the application remains operational without training. On the internal test set (21 samples), the model achieved 100% accuracy with an F1-score of 1.0000 and an inference speed of 404 samples/second. This research is positioned as a proof-of-concept emphasizing the completeness of the transformer-based NLP pipeline and the interpretability of classification results, rather than a claim of state-of-the-art performance. Discussion of limitations and directions for further development are also presented.

W7225084920.abstract: Weight pruning can reduce the storage and inference cost of large language models (LLMs), but preserving quality at high sparsity levels remains challenging. Existing methods face a quality-cost trade-off in this regime. One-shot pruning is cheap but degrades sharply as sparsity increases, even when followed by post-pruning recovery. A growing line of work instead optimizes the mask directly from the dense model under the end-to-end objective; among these methods, [Lee et al.,2026], the recent state of the art at extreme sparsity, reaches high quality but at the cost of model-sized optimizer state and auxiliary variables. To address this gap, we propose ETAPS, which prunes gradually and adapts sparsely: it tightens a global sparsity constraint in progressive stages while training a sparse delta with a small, fixed budget. Our key observation is that gradual weight removal keeps each pruning step small enough for sparse adaptation to compensate, allowing the adapted model to provide end-to-end gradients that guide the next pruning decision without model-sized optimizer state. Across six models from 125M to 13B parameters, ETAPS achieves lower perplexity than ELSA at every evaluated sparsity from 50% to 90%, with perplexity reductions of up to 42%. ETAPS is also far cheaper: at 90% sparsity, it prunes LLaMA2-7B on a single H200, where ELSA uses four, with $5.0\times$ smaller total persistent state and 49% fewer GPU-hours. Together, our findings point to a promising direction for achieving high quality in demanding regimes such as extreme sparsity at substantially lower cost.

W7225131847.abstract: As digital financial services and remote onboarding expand, robust electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC) frameworks have become critical. Concurrently, the rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence facilitates the creation of highly realistic synthetic media, introducing severe vulnerabilities to biometric authentication systems through facial spoofing. Traditional deepfake detection methods typically involve using high-complexity deep neural networks and cloud computing infrastructure which may introduce unacceptable latency, connectivity dependence, computational cost and privacy risks. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the latest innovations in deepfake detection with a particular focus on lightweight deep learning, edge artificial intelligence, model compression and mobile deployment considerations. Various detection methodologies including convolutional neural networks, sequential models, transformer architectures, frequency domain approaches and face liveness analysis are discussed and compared. The survey also covers popular deepfake benchmark datasets and analyze the feasibility of lightweight network architectures such as MobileNet, EfficientNet, ShuffleNet and similar efficient neural networks for e-KYC applications. Model compression techniques, such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation, are assessed with respect to how they affect model complexity, computational cost, processing latency, and detection accuracy. Based on the comparative analysis of the reviewed literature, several research directions are proposed to address the key challenges of cross-dataset generalizability, robustness to adversarial attacks, mobile deployment considerations, energy efficiency, and the accuracy-latency trade-off in real-world mobile e-KYC scenarios.

W7225185805.abstract: Agentic AI (Artificial Intelligence) systems introduce a new class of security risks because they combine large model reasoning with autonomy, memory, planning, tool use, environmental interaction, and, in some cases, multi-agent coordination. These capabilities create various opportunities for adaptive automation and decision support, and they further expand the attack surface beyond conventional model-centric AI security by enabling cascading actions, privilege misuse, adversarial prompt manipulation, memory poisoning, tool-chain compromise, and unsafe behavior under uncertainty. Along these lines, this research addresses the need for formal security risk assessment methods for Agentic AI systems by proposing a modelling framework that integrates static threat, vulnerability, and impact estimation, causal reachability analysis, time varying vulnerability modelling, agent-level expected loss, and threshold-based human override. To demonstrate its applicability, the framework is instantiated in a simulation of an LLM-based autonomous military decision-making system operating under stochastic policy behavior, adversarial jailbreak risk, and command defined risk thresholds. The results show that risk aware filtering can substantially reduce unsafe autonomous actions, increase safe human deferral, and preserve mission success under adversarial and epistemic uncertainty. Through this effort, this study contributes to the development of safer, more transparent, and more accountable autonomous decision-making architectures.

W7225187156.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has revolutionized the ways that automation is applied in the industry, and has introduced new cyber risks, including malware, ransomware, DDoS attacks, insider threats, and advanced persistent threats, as well as the need to connect sensors, controllers, edge devices, and cloud platforms. In this paper, we introduce an Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI) framework to autonomously detect and respond to cyber threats in IIoT applications. It is based on several intelligent agents to continuously monitor, detect anomalies, classify threats, make contextual reasoning, execute automatic responses, and learn. It combines explainable AI and coordinated multi-agent communication to help detect threats in real time, with transparency and accuracy, and minimise response time and false positives. The suggested architecture is scalable, interoperable and is appropriate for the security of the modern industrial automation system.

W7225270506.abstract: Oncology computed tomography (CT) foundation models require large, high-quality training datasets. However, the collection and annotation of such data are costly and time-consuming because tumors occur across multiple anatomical regions and have complex three-dimensional (3D) structures. Strict privacy constraints and institutional variation further limit the availability of large-scale oncology CT datasets. Here, we propose MedGenAgent, a closed-loop agent that supports oncology CT foundation model pretraining in data-constrained settings by iteratively constructing a lesion-rich, anatomically balanced 3D pretraining dataset. MedGenAgent incorporates a Specification resolver tool for structured task parsing and a central Orchestrator tool to coordinate the entire closed-loop agent workflow by leveraging both an Execution layer (including the MAISI synthesis model node for 3D oncology CT sample synthesis, the MedGemma vision-language model node for automated quality control, and the foundation model training node) and a Memory store tool for iterative, feedback-driven updates. Through the synergy of these tools, MedGenAgent synthesized 11,159 CT samples and retained 11,000 quality-controlled samples. By first leveraging this synthetic dataset for pretraining and then aligning with real-world data using only 4400 DeepLesion samples, representing 38.37% of the data used for baseline pretraining, the MedGenAgent-pretrained foundation model achieved performance comparable to the full-data baseline across three retrospective downstream tasks: lesion anatomical site classification, nodule malignancy classification, and cross-institutional NSCLC overall survival classification. Furthermore, automated quality control, independent physician assessment, and workflow analysis demonstrated the construction of a quality-controlled synthetic CT dataset while revealing regional variation in sample quality. Together, these results show that MedGenAgent can autonomously construct quality-controlled synthetic CT data that support the competitive performance of oncology CT foundation models when annotated real-world data are limited.

W7225322389.abstract: Multi-cloud environments have become increasingly important for organizations seeking scalability, resilience, cost optimization, and flexibility across heterogeneous cloud providers. However, managing governance across multiple cloud platforms introduces significant challenges related to security, compliance, configuration consistency, identity management, resource optimization, and policy enforcement. Traditional governance approaches largely depend on static rules, manually configured controls, and centralized monitoring mechanisms, which may be inadequate for highly dynamic cloud infrastructures. This paper proposes an autonomous multi-cloud governance framework based on intelligent agentic artificial intelligence and dynamic policy enforcement. The proposed approach employs autonomous AI agents capable of continuously observing cloud environments, interpreting organizational policies, identifying deviations, reasoning about appropriate responses, and executing corrective actions across heterogeneous cloud platforms. A dynamic policy layer translates governance requirements into machine-enforceable controls while adapting enforcement decisions according to contextual information such as workload characteristics, risk levels, regulatory requirements, and operational conditions. The research methodology combines architectural design, scenario-based experimentation, quantitative evaluation, and comparative analysis. Key evaluation dimensions include policy-compliance accuracy, detection latency, remediation effectiveness, false-positive rates, resource overhead, and cross-cloud consistency. The proposed framework aims to establish a closed governance loop in which perception, reasoning, policy evaluation, action, and continuous learning operate together. Such an approach can strengthen governance automation while reducing administrative effort and improving the responsiveness of multi-cloud security and compliance management.
